Consider the set $A,$ shown above. The boundary of $A$ is given by

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,\,}.
$$

What is the missing expression?
feedback.worked_solution:
The boundary of a set $A,$ denoted $∂A,$ is the set that contains all the boundary points of $A.$

The set $A$ and its boundary $∂A$ are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14041552/assets/eea68ab4e4b440609fcc4f6c2d40c4dc9fc394fc45f1047ec9c658729322749a.png)

From the diagram, the boundary points of $A$ lie on the parabola ${y}^{2}=4x.$

Therefore, 

$$
∂A={(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,{y}^{2}=4x\,}.
$$
